briefs.title: $17B Milestone, Psilocybin's 2027 Runway: Momentum Outpaces the Headwinds
briefs.top: Michigan just crossed $17 billion in lifetime legal cannabis sales and a gubernatorial contender is now campaigning on killing the 24% wholesale tax, giving operators real daylight even as regulators keep the compliance bar high. Nationally, Compass Pathways is racing toward a first-half 2027 psilocybin launch while the DEA rescheduling docket and a wave of Florida M&A keep the sector's growth story intact.
briefs.label: Morning Brief

local.text: Michigan cannabis sales surpass $17 billion lifetime — State CRA data shows the market has topped $17B in combined adult-use and medical sales since regulated sales began, generating an estimated $2.66B in taxes.

GOP governor hopeful now vows to kill wholesale tax — Rep. John James, once a legalization opponent, has pledged to repeal Michigan's 24% wholesale tax after industry executives backed his campaign with checks worth about $90,000.
Menominee petition could add four dispensary licenses — A local ballot drive would raise the city's cannabis retail cap from nine stores to 13, opening fresh licensing runway for operators.

Henry Ford Health lands $1M grant for cannabis-use research — The federal award funds a study to help pregnant Michiganders cut back on marijuana, following data that roughly 16% used cannabis during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

State drops record fine, pulls a vape maker's license — Regulators issued Michigan's largest-ever cannabis fine and revoked the operator's permit over violations described as "egregious," a signal the state is enforcing hard against bad actors while clearing lanes for compliant brands.

national.text: Compass Pathways targets first-half 2027 psilocybin launch — The company expects to finish its rolling NDA submission for COMP360 this quarter as FDA review actively advances toward a treatment-resistant depression approval.

Federal court upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III move — The D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge from rescheduling opponents this month, leaving the medical marijuana reclassification order in effect.

Alabama drops its opposition to federal rescheduling — The state's health department resolved its legal concerns with the DEA process, removing one of the last formal holdouts blocking a Schedule III shift.

Florida cannabis market hit by M&A and listing wave — Trulieve completed a corporate restructuring to list on the NYSE, Vireo Growth is scooping up FLUENT and C21, and Curaleaf just opened its 76th Florida store.

DEA stays quiet on rescheduling guidance for states — California's cannabis regulator says the DEA has shown no interest in helping states prepare, even as the broader Schedule III case awaits a judge's recommendation.
